intro: Check Skarbnik yourself: do something, expect a result, verify it against the chain, not against this page. Level A needs only a browser (5 to 10 minutes, no install). Level B is optional and reproduces things on your machine. The same guide is on the site: https://skarbnik.xyz/#/judge

Everything runs on NEAR testnet, contract kintsugi-l2-cihdp.testnet. On private bounties, researchers and the public never see the secret input. Demo bounties use a public input so anyone can check them.
a_intro: Each step: Do, Expect, Verify, then What this proves and What it does not prove. Transaction links open the testnet explorer.

a.title: Find the contract
a.Expect: a testnet account with a deployed contract and a code hash.
a.Verify: the code hash equals the one the site reads live on https://skarbnik.xyz/#/evidence/contract
a.What this proves: the contract the documents name is deployed on testnet, and the site reads that contract.
a.What it does not prove: that the deployed code is built from this repository; the contract build is not reproducible yet.

a.title: See both sides work: bounty 24 (an AI agent) and bounty 32 (the vendor, with no human)
a.Do: open bounty 24's three calls in order: commit 4G48c6wa…, reveal 3rBVkucS…, proof 9nAK8gi2…. Then bounty 32's reveal HCjck1DL… and proof 9B7FPyju….
a.Expect: on bounty 24, a commit holding only a fingerprint, a reveal that publishes the patch, then a submit_groth16 call that pays 0.11 NEAR (the 0.1 NEAR reward and the agent's own 0.01 NEAR fee back). On bounty 32, a submit_groth16 sent by the vendor's prover account 17 minutes after the reveal, with no human between them.
a.Verify: https://skarbnik.xyz/#/bounties/24 shows "Proof verified" and "Private secret"; the program (data/smooth/) is public, its secret input and reference fix are not in the repository (docs/EVIDENCE.md, "Bounty 24", including how it was checked that the agent could not see the reference fix). https://skarbnik.xyz/#/bounties/32 shows "Proof verified"; the vendor's watch log, with each step's time, the rented GPU and its cost, is in docs/EVIDENCE.md, "The vendor tool".
a.What this proves: the contract paid each attempt only after checking a Groth16 proof that says PASS for that patch, under the published checker; and the vendor side (prove on a rented GPU, wrap, submit) runs on its own.
a.What it does not prove: that the patch is secure beyond this checker's tests; that nothing could have read the private folder (bounty 24's agent ran on the same machine, as the same user); more than a few runs; bounty 32 uses the public demo program, so its fix was known.

a.title: Compare with bounties 16 and 17
a.Do: open bounty 16's proof 5NH9rhRM… and bounty 17's claim BLcWs7dp….
a.Expect: bounty 16 paid by a proof on the public demo bug; bounty 17 paid by claim_timeout, with no submit_groth16 for its attempt.
a.Verify: https://skarbnik.xyz/#/bounties/17 says "Timeout settlement" and "Why this is not “Proof verified”": the laptop proof was too slow for the 4 hour window. Bounty 24 was the same kind of task, proven on a GPU instead.
a.What this proves: proof-checked and timeout payouts are kept apart, and a silent vendor does not block payment.
a.What it does not prove: that bounty 17's fix passed; the timeout pays without any verdict.

a.title: See a proof pay and a proof fail on the same bounty
a.Do: open bounty 1's PASS CczggiUN… and FAIL 6B9ocDas….
a.Expect: two submit_groth16 calls of about 36 Tgas; only the PASS moves NEAR.
a.Verify: they are different attempts on the same bounty.
a.What this proves: the contract applies the verdict inside the proof: a PASS pays, a FAIL spends the attempt.
a.What it does not prove: that every forged proof is refused; the attacks tried are listed in docs/SECURITY.md.

a.title: Compare the checker id
a.Do: read the allowlist with any view call to get_allowed_image_ids (or docs/TRY_IT.md, step 2).
a.Verify: it equals the image id inside bounty 24's proof (the site's Checker tab; Level B rebuilds it from source).
a.What this proves: new bounties can only use this one checker, and bounty 24 was decided by it.
a.What it does not prove: that the id is built from this source (B5 shows that) or that the checker has no bugs.

a.title: Read what is not claimed
a.Do: open https://skarbnik.xyz/#/evidence/limits or the README's "Trust assumptions" (every limit: docs/CLAIMS.md, "Known limits").
a.Expect: plain limits, among them: no external audit (only AI review passes), a full access key kept on purpose on the testnet contract (an experimental contract; the mainnet contract is planned without one), testnet only.
a.Verify: the access key with a view_access_key_list call on kintsugi-l2-cihdp.testnet, and the live code hash against the last deploy in docs/EVIDENCE.md, "Contract code and every deploy".
a.What this proves: the limits are published, and the full access key can be seen on chain.
a.What it does not prove: that the list is complete; no one outside the project has audited the contract.

b_intro: Commands run from the root of a clone of the repository. The judge bounties for B2 and B3 are 27 to 31 (K = 2, at most 1 attempt per account, 41 h verdict window); 18 to 22 are retired. What each step needs:

b.shows: Read bounties and the allowlist from the chain (docs/TRY_IT.md, steps 1 to 3)
b.Expect: bounty 7 is Level 2, open and opened by its Proof 0; the allowlist prints MATCH; the judge bounties show opened or closed.
b.What this proves: the chain holds what the documents say.

b.shows: Open a closed judge bounty with a real proof from your own account (docs/TRY_IT.md, step 5)
b.needs: near-cli-rs 0.30.1, a testnet account from the faucet (free); about 35 Tgas of testnet gas
b.Expect: the return value "opened", a bounty_opened event naming your account, about 35 Tgas.
b.What this proves: any account can make the contract check a real Groth16 proof on chain.
b.What it does not prove: anything about attempts; it reuses bounty 17's Proof 0.

b.shows: See a proof refused at the pairing check itself (docs/TRY_IT.md, step 6)
b.Expect: "the Groth16 proof does not verify for this bounty's image id and this journal", about 34.9 Tgas.
b.What this proves: a wrong seal is refused by the pairing check itself, after every cheaper check passed.
b.What it does not prove: that every other kind of forgery is refused (see the attacks in docs/SECURITY.md).

b.shows: Run the contract tests: cargo test -p kintsugi-contract (docs/TRY_IT.md, step 8)
b.download: the contract's crates, about 3 minutes the first time
b.What this proves: the contract's rules behave as the tests say, including bounty 1's two real proofs checked natively.
b.What it does not prove: behaviour on chain (B2 and B3 show that); the tests were written by the same team.

b.shows: Rebuild the checker and compare its image id: ./scripts/check_image_id.sh kintsugi-l2-cihdp.testnet 17 (docs/TRY_IT.md, step 9)
b.needs: Docker with buildx, RISC Zero's toolchain, about 10 GB of free disk
b.download: RISC Zero's guest builder image, 7.46 GB
b.memory: a few GB for the build container
b.What this proves: the checker id on chain is built from this source.
b.What it does not prove: that the checker is free of bugs or that its checks are enough.

b.shows: Verify a stored proof: cargo build --release -p skarbnik-host, then ./target/release/skarbnik-host verify docs/evidence/receipts/bounty17_proof0_groth16.bin (docs/TRY_IT.md, step 10)
b.Expect: VALID, and a journal sha256 equal to bounty 17's proof0_journal_hash on chain.
b.What this proves: the stored proof verifies on your machine for the published id, and its journal is the one recorded on chain.
b.What it does not prove: anything about the secret input or about later attempts.

b.shows: The agent's checks without a model key: ./scripts/agent_dry_run_test.sh
b.needs: Rust with the wasm32-unknown-unknown target, agent/config.local.toml from ./scripts/agent_testnet.sh setup (a testnet account)
b.Expect: 11 of 11 checks pass, and nothing is sent.
b.What this proves: the agent refuses a key not limited to commit and reveal, overspending, and a fix that reads files or the environment.
b.What it does not prove: that a model writes good fixes.

b.shows: Verify the contract yourself: rebuild it from its commit with cargo near build reproducible-wasm and compare with the code hash on chain (docs/TRY_IT.md, step 11)
b.Expect: sha256 ecf697be619d5dc730de58853ae3daa65bff3ac1a23804a1c390663ca059421e, whose base58 form Gx1JfW7GdpD7sgWf2JwvQhQzfrGy5CnMZyTW2bvFBX6u equals the contract's code hash on chain.
b.What this proves: the code running on chain is built from the published commit c74bd5c, so reading that source is reading the contract.
b.What it does not prove: that the source is free of bugs, or that the owner will not deploy other code later (the testnet contract keeps its full access key on purpose; every deploy is listed in docs/EVIDENCE.md).

b_notes: Expected results are written next to each command in docs/TRY_IT.md, with the run that produced them in docs/EVIDENCE.md. No step needs real money or a mainnet wallet.
Do not start a full vendor proof as part of a review: one attempt takes 1.5 to 4 hours on a laptop CPU, and the Groth16 step needs about 7 GiB of memory (docs/numbers.md).
claims_intro: Each claim carries one label. Implemented: in the code and covered by tests. Demonstrated: done on testnet, with transactions. Experimental: tried once, or on a different setup. Planned: not built. A claim with no evidence is never shown as done.
